38605609.clinical_problem: adolescent idiopathic scoliosis diagnosis and Cobb angle measurement
38605609.patient_population: adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis undergoing full-length standing spine radiographs
38605609.model_description: Input is a full-length standing spinal X-ray; the model detects key points and outputs a scoliosis diagnosis/classification and Cobb angle measurement. Trained and tested on 748 retrospectively collected images (602 train/validate, 146 test).
38605609.headline_result: 94.5% diagnostic/classification accuracy; 94.9% of Cobb angle measurements within clinically acceptable range (mean absolute difference 2.1 degrees, r2>=0.9552)

38605612.clinical_problem: image quality control of pediatric pelvic radiographs (for DDH assessment)
38605612.model_description: Input is an anteroposterior pediatric pelvic radiograph; the model outputs a quality assessment (pelvic tilt and rotation indices) to flag images unsuitable for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) evaluation. Trained on a random split of the cohort.

38627421.model_family: neural network ("boosted division time attribute extraction"/TAE-PIS)
38627421.clinical_problem: detection of fetal/pediatric brain tumor (glioblastoma) on MRI
38627421.patient_population: children/fetuses with suspected brain tumor glioblastoma (abstract poorly specifies cohort)
38627421.model_description: Input is brain MRI; the method segments and classifies images to recognize glioblastoma, comparing a proposed max/min rationalization and attribute-extraction approach against genetic algorithm, CNN, fuzzy min-max and SVM baselines. The abstract text is unusually garbled and does not clearly describe a real patient cohort or training pipeline.

38641580.clinical_problem: autonomous fetal morphology scan (view-plane and organ labeling for congenital anomaly detection)
38641580.model_description: Input is real-time fetal ultrasound video; the system first differentiates fetal view planes, then labels and segments internal organs (tested on the fetal abdomen) using a deep learning/clustering merger combined with YOLOv8 segmentation, intended as decision support alongside the sonographer.
38641580.dataset_size: not stated (fetal abdomen ultrasound image dataset)
38641580.headline_result: System correctly labeled view plane and corresponding organs on real-time ultrasound movies (no numeric performance given)
38641580.study_design: clinical trial / technical development (registered trial PARADISE, NCT05738954)

38708929.clinical_problem: fetal growth restriction assessment from placental imaging
38708929.model_description: Editorial commentary on a hybrid model that performs automatic placental radiomics from T2-weighted MRI combined with multifeature fusion to assess fetal growth restriction. No abstract text was provided, so the model itself is not described here.

38744197.model_family: graph neural network post-processing of DNN segmentation (U-Net, UNETr, MSGSE-Net backbones)
38744197.clinical_problem: segmentation of basal ganglia after early brain lesion (neonatal arterial ischemic stroke)
38744197.patient_population: healthy children and children after neonatal arterial ischemic stroke (NAIS)
38744197.model_description: Input is brain MRI of healthy children or children after neonatal stroke; a deep neural network (one of three backbones) produces an initial basal ganglia segmentation, which a graph neural network then refines using spatial/class-probability graphs to improve consistency in the presence of lesions.
38744197.dataset_size: not stated (small training datasets typical of pediatric/rare pathology)
38744197.headline_result: Median Dice improved up to 4%; median Hausdorff distance reduced up to 93% in healthy children (36.45 to 2.57) and up to 91% in NAIS children (40.64 to 3.50)

38796378.clinical_problem: identification of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) marrow involvement from brain MRI
38796378.patient_population: children with ALL and normal children (604 brain MRI studies)
38796378.model_description: Input is a T1-weighted brain MRI image with a manually delineated region of interest along the clivus; a radiomics model (SVM on extracted features) and a separate deep learning model (EfficientNet-B3) each output a classification distinguishing ALL from normal children.
38796378.dataset_size: 604 brain MRI studies (ALL and normal children)
38796378.headline_result: AUC 0.981 (deep learning) vs 0.962 (radiomics) in the testing cohort; accuracy 0.934/sensitivity 0.870/specificity 0.974 for deep learning model

38801074.exclusion_reason: brain tumor MRI classification study with no stated pediatric population

38840982.clinical_problem: rib fracture detection on pediatric chest radiographs
38840982.patient_population: pediatric chest radiographs (704 unique subjects; 2,800 fracture-present and 2,800 fracture-absent patches)
38840982.model_description: Input is a patch from a pediatric chest radiograph; a modified cycleGAN (using "near-pair" fracture-present/absent regions from the same subject plus a realism loss term) generates synthetic fracture-present images with known fracture location, which are added to the training set of a YOLOv5 rib-fracture object detector. Output is a bounding box indicating a suspected fracture.
38840982.dataset_size: 2,800 fracture-present and 2,800 fracture-absent image patches from 704 pediatric chest radiographs
38840982.headline_result: Object detector recall 0.57 and F2 0.59 when trained on 500 real + 500 synthetic radiographs, vs. recall 0.49 and F2 0.53 with 500 real radiographs alone; synthetic images rated 2.5/5 vs 4.1/5 (real fracture) on Likert fracture-likelihood scale by 4 pediatric radiologists
38840982.study_design: retrospective technical development with observer study

38895379.model_family: hierarchical clustering of resting-state fMRI functional connectivity
38895379.clinical_problem: how infant brain language-network connectivity relates to later reading ability
38895379.patient_population: 76 infants followed longitudinally to kindergarten (41 further assessed for emergent word reading)
38895379.model_description: Input is infant resting-state fMRI; hierarchical clustering is used to identify a modular language network, and functional connectivity of network modules is then related (via mediation models) to later kindergarten phonological skills and word-reading ability. This is a developmental-neuroscience application of unsupervised learning rather than a diagnostic imaging tool.
38895379.release_evidence: research/longitudinal cohort study, no software or model release stated
38895379.headline_result: Inferior frontal module connectivity prospectively correlated with kindergarten phonological skills and emergent word reading (mediation significant, exact stats not given as effect sizes in abstract)

38922421.clinical_problem: quantification of cerebral venous circulation to assess hypoxic-ischemic risk in neonates
38922421.patient_population: 317 neonates with or without risk of cerebral hypoxia-ischemia
38922421.model_description: Input is susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) MRI of the neonatal brain; a deep learning segmentation algorithm automatically detects and quantifies deep medullary veins (number, width, curvature), which are then compared across sex, prematurity, hypoxic-ischemia risk group, and hemorrhage status.
38922421.headline_result: Significant differences in DMV number/width/curvature by sex, prematurity, risk group and hemorrhage status (e.g., width greater in low- vs high-risk group, p<0.01)

38946976.model_family: autoencoder with reconstruction regularization (vs. MLP and classical ML)
38946976.clinical_problem: prediction of fluid intelligence from structural brain MRI in early adolescence
38946976.patient_population: 11,534 adolescents aged 9-10 from the ABCD Data Release 3.0
38946976.model_description: Input is 604 FreeSurfer-derived structural features from T1-weighted MRI across 148 regions of interest; an autoencoder model with reconstruction regularization outputs a predicted fluid intelligence score, benchmarked against MLP and classical machine learning models, with SHAP used to rank feature importance.
38946976.headline_result: Best model achieved Pearson correlation 0.209 +/- 0.02 and MSE 105.212 +/- 2.53 for predicting fluid intelligence; performance better in female than male adolescents
38946976.study_design: retrospective secondary analysis of ABCD cohort

38968007.exclusion_reason: non-imaging: gestational age/preterm birth prediction from blood metabolite and clinical variables, no radiologic imaging

39025919.model_family: DenseNet-121 and EfficientNet-v2-M convolutional neural networks
39025919.clinical_problem: postnatal age estimation of infants from skull radiographs
39025919.model_description: Input is an anteroposterior or lateral plain skull radiograph of an infant under 12 months; the CNN models output a predicted postnatal age, with gradient-weighted class activation mapping (Grad-CAM) used to highlight the cranial sutures and structures driving the prediction.

39051284.clinical_problem: segmentation of thigh muscle and subcutaneous fat in muscular dystrophy for quantitative follow-up
39051284.patient_population: adult and pediatric patients with muscular dystrophies undergoing bilateral thigh MRI (23 patients)
39051284.model_description: Input is a T1-weighted out-of-phase thigh MRI; U-Net models automatically segment subcutaneous adipose tissue and either the thigh muscles as a whole (U-Net1) or the three muscular compartments separately (U-Net3), compared against manual radiologist segmentation.
39051284.headline_result: Dice similarity coefficient: U-Net1 96.8/95.3/95.6% (train/validation/test) for SAT; U-Net3 accuracy 94.1/92.9/93.9%; median DSC 0.95 for SAT segmentation

39055472.exclusion_reason: not radiologic imaging AI: 2D video motion-capture analysis of kicking motion, ultrasound used only as the reference diagnostic standard

39060414.model_family: deep learning with adaptive instance normalization (AdaIN) style transfer
39060414.patient_population: children and adolescents undergoing hand radiography (RSNA public dataset, 1-228 months; private dataset, 12-218 months)
39060414.model_description: Input is a hand radiograph; DASA-net combines age and sex distributions via adaptive instance normalization and style transfer to simulate comparing the hand image with a standard bone atlas, outputting a predicted bone age. Evaluated against BoneXpert, Deeplasia, BoNet and other deep learning methods.
39060414.dataset_size: 14,236 hand radiographs (RSNA dataset); 474 hand radiographs (private Zigong dataset, 268 male)
39060414.headline_result: Mean absolute deviation 3.52 months on RSNA dataset and 3.82 months on private dataset, outperforming BoneXpert, Deeplasia and BoNet
39060414.study_design: retrospective model development with external dataset validation

39110559.model_family: CNN-driven deformable model (learned energy function + explicit deformable surface)
39110559.body_region: fetal head; also left ventricle, left atrium, bladder (mixed pediatric/adult tasks)
39110559.clinical_problem: 3D anatomical segmentation from limited training data, evaluated in part on fetal head segmentation on ultrasound
39110559.patient_population: mixed: includes fetal head ultrasound segmentation alongside adult left ventricle/atrium and bladder segmentation tasks
39110559.model_description: A CNN learns an energy function from localized anatomical image patches that drives an explicit deformable surface model to segment 3D structures with limited training data. One of several evaluation tasks is fetal head segmentation on ultrasound, alongside adult cardiac and bladder segmentation on MRI/CT.
39110559.dataset_size: varying numbers of training volumes per task (not specified for fetal head task)
39110559.headline_result: Outperformed state-of-the-art deep-learning segmentation methods across all tasks when few training samples were available (no single fetal-head-specific number given)

39167304.exclusion_reason: general review of deep learning for PET/MR across all ages; pediatric PET/MR mentioned only as one of several unmet-need bullet points, not the review's focus

39176809.body_region: fetal heart / whole fetus (delivery room monitoring)
39176809.clinical_problem: prediction of fetal acidosis at delivery
39176809.patient_population: 2,266 deliveries at a tertiary hospital delivery room
39176809.model_description: Inputs are features extracted from electronic medical records, biosignals (cardiotocography) and imaging data (including fetal echocardiography), concatenated into a single feature vector; a classifier trained on this multimodal input outputs a predicted probability of post-delivery fetal acidosis.

39176918.clinical_problem: prenatal detection of congenital heart disease
39176918.patient_population: fetuses screened for congenital heart disease across 28 studies included in the review
39176918.model_description: A PRISMA systematic review of 28 studies (from 621 screened) on AI applications for prenatal detection of congenital heart disease, finding deep learning as the predominant approach and ultrasound and MRI as the main data types used, summarizing the landscape of available data and methods.

39214549.exclusion_reason: non-imaging: cerebral palsy prediction from perinatal/maternal registry variables, no imaging data used

39219825.exclusion_reason: dental/oral radiology bibliometric analysis, not a radiology-AI application study

39250874.model_family: mixed effect random forest (MERF) longitudinal machine learning
39250874.clinical_problem: prediction of low and very low birth weight from prenatal ultrasound measurements
39250874.patient_population: pregnant women with serial prenatal ultrasound biometry measurements
39250874.model_description: Input is longitudinal prenatal ultrasound biometric measurements; a mixed effect random forest model (compared against other longitudinal and standard machine learning methods) outputs predicted birth weight and classifies low/very low birth weight status, with an interpretable-tree method used to extract risk features.
39250874.headline_result: Mixed effect random forest gave the best overall performance for birth weight prediction and LBW/VLBW classification (no single summary statistic given)

39253631.clinical_problem: tractography (white matter fiber reconstruction) of the fetal brain in utero
39253631.patient_population: fetuses aged 23-36 weeks gestation (11 test scans; trained on manually-refined whole-brain fetal tractograms)
39253631.model_description: Input is diffusion-weighted MRI of the fetal brain (voxel-wise fiber orientation, propagation history, spatial and tissue-segmentation information, and an atlas prior); a deep neural network with convolutional and attention modules outputs streamline tractograms of white matter fiber pathways, with anatomically constrained filtering to prune implausible streamlines.
39253631.headline_result: Achieved superior performance across all evaluated tracts compared to prior methods (no single summary metric given in abstract)

39253642.model_family: machine learning-assisted symbolic regression (regional cortical growth model)
39253642.clinical_problem: how regional brain tissue growth shapes cortical folding patterns in development
39253642.patient_population: 735 pediatric subjects (prenatal to 24 months), over 1,000 MRI scans
39253642.model_description: Longitudinal MRI-derived surface expansion and cortical thickness data from prenatal and infant brains are used to fit machine learning-assisted symbolic regression growth models for cortical regions; these models drive computational simulations of brain folding, compared to conventional uniform-growth models using curvature, sulcal depth and gyrification metrics.
39253642.dataset_size: over 1,000 MRI scans from 735 pediatric subjects (29 post-menstrual weeks to 24 months)
39253642.headline_result: Regional growth models produced folding patterns that more closely matched real brain structure than conventional uniform growth models (qualitative and quantitative comparison, no single summary statistic given)

39260905.exclusion_reason: general developmental-psychology review of measurement technologies (eye-tracking, MRI, AI); not focused on a radiology-AI model

39263498.model_family: AI motion-artifact suppression algorithm (vendor-supplied, not further specified)
39263498.clinical_problem: pitfall of AI-based motion artifact suppression mimicking an osteochondral lesion
39263498.patient_population: a young child imaged for suspected knee pathology
39263498.model_description: Case report in which an AI-based motion-artifact-suppression algorithm applied to a child's knee MRI removed most (not all) of a linear motion artifact, creating an appearance mimicking an osteochondral lesion; the case illustrates the need to review both original and AI-enhanced images.

39272716.exclusion_reason: case report of juvenile osteochondritis dissecans; AI mentioned only as a future prospect, no AI model applied or evaluated

39279845.model_family: U-Net-based deep neural network (fiber orientation distribution estimation)
39279845.clinical_problem: estimating white matter fiber orientation distributions in neonatal brains from limited diffusion MRI
39279845.model_description: Input is diffusion-weighted MRI of the neonatal brain; a U-Net architecture is trained to estimate fiber orientation distributions (FODs) using either multi-shell multi-tissue (MSMT-CSD) or single-shell three-tissue (SS3T-CSD) constrained spherical deconvolution as ground truth, comparing which ground-truth choice generalizes better across acquisition protocols and ages.
39279845.headline_result: SS3T-CSD ground truth gave more realistic single/multi-fiber voxel ratios and more robust performance across age groups than MSMT-CSD, especially with more input gradient directions

39301479.clinical_problem: classification of pediatric chest radiographs as normal vs. cardiopulmonary disease
39301479.model_description: Input is a pediatric chest radiograph; a modality-specific pretext encoder (trained via denoising/deblurring on chest X-rays, VGG-16-Sharp-U-Net) feeds a classification head to output normal vs. cardiopulmonary-disease classification, compared to standard ImageNet transfer learning, with a fuzzy ensemble of pretext-learned models.
39301479.headline_result: Ensemble balanced accuracy 0.6376, sensitivity 0.4991, F-score 0.5102 vs. ImageNet-pretrained baseline balanced accuracy 0.5654, sensitivity 0.1983, F-score 0.2977

39314513.clinical_problem: tissue segmentation, white matter tract segmentation and cortical parcellation of the fetal brain
39314513.model_description: Input is diffusion-weighted fetal brain MRI; a unified multi-task deep learning model simultaneously (1) segments brain tissue into white matter, gray matter and CSF, (2) segments 31 white matter tracts, and (3) parcellates the cortex and deep gray/white matter into 96 anatomical regions, trained on manually/semi-automatically annotated fetal brains.
39314513.headline_result: Mean Dice similarity coefficient 0.865 (tissue segmentation), 0.825 (white matter tract segmentation), 0.819 (parcellation)

39411546.model_family: deep learning with a cardiac-cyclic loss function
39411546.clinical_problem: diagnosis of fetal arrhythmia from echocardiography
39411546.model_description: Input is an M-mode fetal echocardiogram image; a deep learning network with a novel loss term based on cardiac cyclic information predicts peak points used to classify fetal arrhythmia into four categories, compared against baseline networks without the cyclic loss.
39411546.headline_result: Cyclic loss improved F1-score by 7.11-14.81% across network combinations (18.2% improvement in the low-quality image subgroup); average 20.6% improvement in four-category diagnostic precision

39413238.clinical_problem: computer-aided detection of lung nodules on low-dose pediatric chest CT
39413238.model_description: Editorial comment ("a cautionary tale") discussing computer-aided detection of lung nodules on low-dose pediatric chest CT. No abstract text was provided, so the underlying study's methods and results are not described here.

39424912.exclusion_reason: published erratum/author correction notice, no abstract content

39429804.model_family: machine learning model trained on Gompertz growth-curve parameters
39429804.clinical_problem: prediction of birth weight from fetal ultrasound biometry
39429804.patient_population: 774 pregnant women (Seethapathy cohort, Chennai, India, 2015-2017); validated on an independent cohort of 365 women
39429804.model_description: Input is fetal biometry (femur length, head circumference, abdominal circumference, biparietal diameter) fitted with a Gompertz growth model per fetus; the fetus-specific Gompertz scale parameter (inferable from ultrasound data by 24-35 weeks) feeds a machine learning model that outputs predicted birth weight, without requiring late-term ultrasound.
39429804.dataset_size: 774 pregnant women (development cohort); 365 women (independent validation cohort)
39429804.headline_result: Birth weight prediction error <8% on the development cohort and 8.4% on the independent validation cohort, outperforming published methods using late-term ultrasound
39429804.study_design: prospective cohort study with independent external validation

39467890.model_family: center-point detection-based vertebra localization and tilt estimation network
39467890.clinical_problem: automated Cobb angle estimation for scoliosis assessment
39467890.patient_population: 118 cases (342 Cobb angle measurements) including children and adolescents with scoliosis
39467890.model_description: Input is a spinal radiograph; the center-point-based VLTENet localizes vertebrae and estimates tilt to compute Cobb angles, compared against the keypoint-based VFLDNet model, using manual consensus measurement as reference.
39467890.headline_result: MAE 2.15 degrees (total Cobb angle) and 1.89 degrees (major curve) vs. VFLDNet's 2.80 and 2.57 degrees; kappa 0.83 vs. 0.67 for major curve classification
39467890.study_design: retrospective diagnostic accuracy with external validation dataset

39473785.model_family: 2D convolutional autoencoder (2DCNN-AE) with multi-sequence and multi-scale asynchronous correlation learning
39473785.clinical_problem: assessment of mental/behavioral health risk in adolescents from fMRI
39473785.patient_population: 174 individuals aged 17-22 from the Adolescent Health Risk Behavior (AHRB) dataset
39473785.model_description: Input is fMRI data from adolescents/young adults; a 2D convolutional autoencoder combined with multi-scale asynchronous correlation feature extraction outputs a classification of health risk behavior status, compared against conventional benchmark models.
39473785.headline_result: Precision 83.116%, recall 84.784%, F1-score 83.942%, surpassing standard benchmarks

39525051.model_family: spectral graph-based sample weighting for predictive models
39525051.clinical_problem: modeling heterogeneous predictability of imaging-based risk models across sub-cohorts (e.g., adolescent alcohol-use risk)
39525051.patient_population: adolescents from the NCANDA cohort (alcohol-initiation task) and adults from ADNI (dementia task)
39525051.model_description: Imaging and demographic/neuropsychological features feed a predictive model; subject-specific sample weights are modeled as a linear combination of eigenbases of a spectral population graph encoding factor similarity across subjects, applied to predicting initiation of heavy drinking in adolescents (NCANDA) and to distinguishing dementia from MCI in an adult cohort (ADNI).
39525051.headline_result: Sample weighting scheme improved interpretability and highlighted sub-cohorts with distinct predictability compared to existing weighting schemes (no single summary accuracy given)

39525517.model_family: analysis of ultrasound machine zoom-level metadata (non-image classification)
39525517.clinical_problem: automatic recognition of anatomical structures during fetal ultrasound scanning
39525517.model_description: During fetal ultrasound scanning, sonographers zoom in/out on structures of interest; this study explores whether the zoom pattern itself (rather than the image content) forms a signature that can classify which fetal anatomical structure is being examined, without a convolutional neural network reading the images directly.

39538049.model_family: deep learning-based brain region segmentation toolkit
39538049.clinical_problem: quantitative reference for pediatric brain structural (gray/white matter, cortical) development
39538049.patient_population: 312 healthy children aged 1.5-14.5 years (210 boys, 102 girls), divided into five age groups
39538049.model_description: Input is high-resolution T1-weighted structural brain MRI; an established deep-learning-based segmentation toolkit segments brain regions, from which gray and white matter volumes, cortical thickness and surface area are computed and compared across age groups and sex to build a normative growth reference.
39538049.headline_result: Gray/white matter and total brain volume increased with age; cortical thickness and surface area decreased with age (no single accuracy metric, this is a normative reference study)

39600061.exclusion_reason: general clinical review of point-of-care ultrasound in pediatric AKI; AI mentioned only in passing as a general technology trend

39657530.clinical_problem: sex differences in emotion-related brain function during adolescence
39657530.patient_population: adolescents undergoing fMRI (plus simulated data and an EEG dataset for generalizability testing)
39657530.model_description: Input is dynamic functional connectivity (high-dimensional) and brain activation (low-dimensional) data; a tensor dictionary-based heterogeneous transfer learning framework transfers knowledge between the two feature spaces to improve classification of sex differences in adolescent emotion-related brain activity, also tested on simulated and EEG data.
39657530.headline_result: Incorporating prior knowledge via the proposed framework significantly enhanced classification performance for gender classification from fMRI (no single summary metric given)

39674995.model_family: CNN and U-Net-based signal/image processing pipeline
39674995.clinical_problem: automated measurement of migration percentage (hip displacement severity) in cerebral palsy
39674995.patient_population: children with cerebral palsy undergoing hip ultrasound (62 hips)
39674995.model_description: Input is coronal and transverse hip ultrasound scans; a pipeline combining signal filtering, CNNs and U-Nets segments the region of interest, detects edges/feature points and selects frames to automatically compute migration percentage on ultrasound, validated against manual migration percentage on hip radiographs.
39674995.dataset_size: 62 hips (36 training with augmentation, 8 validation, 18 testing)
39674995.headline_result: ICC(2,1) 0.86 and mean absolute difference 6.5% +/- 5.5% between automated ultrasound-based and manual radiograph-based migration percentage; average 104 seconds per hip

39698615.model_family: Inception-v3 and graph convolutional network (with graph attention, 3D patch-based)
39698615.clinical_problem: prediction/classification of neonatal hyperbilirubinemia severity from brain MRI
39698615.model_description: Input is neonatal brain MRI; Inception-v3, a standard graph convolutional network, and a proposed 3D patch-based graph convolutional network with graph attention each classify images by serum bilirubin threshold group to detect neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (NHB), evaluated by AUC, accuracy, sensitivity and specificity.
39698615.headline_result: AUC 0.86 and accuracy 0.81 for the proposed 3D patch-based GCN at a bilirubin threshold of 400 micromol/L, versus 72-78.3% accuracy for other models

39715470.model_family: contrast-agnostic machine learning-based brain volumetry tool
39715470.clinical_problem: distinguishing transient from persistent brain structural changes (ventricular enlargement) in pediatric ADEM
39715470.patient_population: 61 pediatric patients with acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (39 MOG-antibody-positive) from a multicenter cohort, compared with 1,219 pediatric healthy controls
39715470.model_description: Input is routine clinical brain MRI; a contrast-agnostic machine-learning-based volumetry tool computes volumes of multiple brain structures (including cerebral ventricles and deep gray matter), which are analyzed longitudinally with mixed-effect models to distinguish patients whose ventricular volume expansion resolves from those with persistent expansion and brain atrophy.
39715470.dataset_size: 61 pediatric ADEM patients vs. 1,219 pediatric healthy controls
39715470.headline_result: 12/22 patients with >2 MRI scans resolved ventricular volume expansion, 10/22 had persistent expansion; persistent-expansion patients had greater reductions in deep gray matter volume and more residual neurologic signs

39758885.model_family: SVM classification, tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS), and canonical correlation analysis (CCA) on HARDI diffusion models
39758885.clinical_problem: identifying white matter markers of preterm birth
39758885.patient_population: 46 preterm babies at term-equivalent age and 23 term-born control neonates
39758885.model_description: Input is High Angular Resolution Diffusion Imaging (HARDI) of the neonatal brain; multiple advanced diffusion microstructural models are analyzed with a univariate inferential method (TBSS), a univariate predictive method (SVM classification) and a multivariate predictive method (CCA) to identify white-matter differences discriminating preterm from term-born neonates.
39758885.headline_result: TBSS found significant differences in multiple white matter areas; SVM classification on skeletonized HARDI measures achieved satisfactory accuracy, particularly for fiber-directionality parameters (no single overall accuracy figure given)

39816514.model_family: deep learning cascaded convolutional registration networks + multi-atlas segmentation (nnU-Net comparison)
39816514.clinical_problem: registration and segmentation of fetal brain MRI to support neurodevelopmental abnormality detection
39816514.patient_population: fetal brain MRI (dataset size not stated)
39816514.model_description: Input is fetal brain MRI; a cascade of convolutional networks predicts incremental deformation fields at multiple spatial-frequency levels to register images, which is then integrated into a multi-atlas segmentation pipeline requiring only a small set of annotated atlas images, and compared against nnU-Net.
39816514.release_evidence: Pipeline for registration and multi-atlas segmentation is publicly available at https://github.com/ValBcn/CasReg
39816514.dataset_size: not stated (small subset of annotated atlas images)
39816514.headline_result: Outperformed existing state-of-the-art registration techniques, including other multi-resolution strategies, by a substantial margin; competitive with nnU-Net using only a small atlas subset

40039735.patient_population: pediatric and adult patients undergoing brain MRI
40039735.model_description: Input is brain MRI; a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model learns to reconstruct healthy brain MRI and generates anomaly maps from the reconstruction error, used to classify a scan as healthy or unhealthy and localize abnormal regions, compared against a GAN-based generative baseline.
40039735.headline_result: Model correctly differentiated all healthy vs. unhealthy test patients; anomaly map Dice coefficient 0.376, outperforming a GAN baseline

40040150.model_family: variational Gaussian process latent variable model (unsupervised probabilistic shape matching)
40040150.clinical_problem: establishing correspondences between brain structure shapes to monitor anatomical change in pediatric disease
40040150.model_description: Input is brain structure surface descriptors derived from pediatric MRI; an unsupervised variational framework based on a Gaussian process latent variable model learns group-wise latent representations to establish shape correspondences between brain structures, intended to help quantify anatomical change in healthy and abnormal pediatric brains.
40040150.headline_result: Model captured non-linearities in nonrigid brain structures on real-world neurodevelopmental data (no single quantitative summary given)

40085041.model_family: support vector machine (compared with random forest, current reality tree, linear regression)
40085041.clinical_problem: bone age estimation from wrist MRI in adolescent males
40085041.patient_population: 124 Han male adolescents aged 6.0-18.0 years from Shanghai, Zhejiang and Jiangsu, China
40085041.model_description: Input is wrist MRI (T1WI/T2WI) with graded and measured epiphyseal development at the distal radius/ulna and metacarpals, combined with height and weight; a support vector machine (best of several models tested) outputs a predicted bone age.
40085041.headline_result: SVM accuracy within 1.0 year of true age 88.7%, within 1.5 years 96.0%

41367399.model_family: deep learning phenotype encoder with domain-adversarial training + growth predictor
41367399.clinical_problem: prediction of normal and pathologic head shape development for surgical planning
41367399.patient_population: pediatric patients including those with cranial pathology, imaged with cross-sectional CT and 3D photograms
41367399.model_description: Input is a cross-sectional head CT or 3D photogram segmentation; a phenotype encoder creates age- and sex-independent patient representations, and a growth predictor generates the predicted head shape at any target age/sex, accounting for pathology, without requiring longitudinal training data. Evaluated against an independent longitudinal dataset.
41367399.dataset_size: not stated (cross-sectional CT and 3D photogram training set; independent longitudinal test set)
41367399.headline_result: Head surface growth prediction error 4.93 +/- 2.29 mm and volumetric error 0.16 +/- 0.11 L in cranial-pathology patients; 4.61 +/- 3.28 mm and 0.27 +/- 0.19 L in normative subjects
41367399.study_design: retrospective technical development with independent longitudinal validation

42040038.exclusion_reason: narrative review of dental/orthodontic imaging (CBCT, panoramic radiography); AI is mentioned only briefly as an emerging technology

42040039.exclusion_reason: narrative review of pediatric dental/orthodontic radiology; discusses AI-assisted panoramic radiograph tools but review is centered on dental imaging, excluded as non-radiologic

36706870.clinical_problem: effect of radiation therapy on short-range white matter connectivity in childhood brain tumor survivors
36706870.patient_population: 26 childhood brain tumor (medulloblastoma) survivors and 26 typically developing children
36706870.model_description: Input is T1-weighted and diffusion-weighted MRI, from which short-range white matter connections are delineated by a whole-brain virtual dissection approach; a random forest classifier identifies which short-range connections show the largest microstructural (fractional anisotropy, axial diffusivity) differences between brain tumor survivors and typically developing children.
36706870.dataset_size: 26 brain tumor survivors and 26 typically developing children
36706870.headline_result: Random forest classifier distinguished patients from controls using short-range white matter microstructure with 87.5% accuracy

36802769.model_family: random forest and other machine learning classifiers
36802769.clinical_problem: automated quality assessment of pediatric dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) MRI perfusion data
36802769.patient_population: pediatric normal-brain DSC-MRI cases (1,027 signal-time courses)
36802769.model_description: Input is a DSC-MRI signal-time course; quantitative quality measures (signal drop-to-noise ratio, RMSE, FWHM, percentage signal recovery) are computed and used to train machine learning classifiers (random forest performing best) that automatically flag data quality, replacing manual qualitative review.
36802769.dataset_size: 1,027 signal-time courses (243 double-reviewed for inter-rater comparison)
36802769.headline_result: Random forest classifier achieved sensitivity 0.94, specificity 0.83, precision 0.93, classification error 9.3%, AUC 0.89

36834149.exclusion_reason: clinical/fitness-variable (BMI, handgrip strength) prediction model for bone mineral density; not an imaging-based AI model, DXA used only as the ground-truth label

36840982.exclusion_reason: letter/correspondence with no abstract text provided

36890823.exclusion_reason: published erratum notice, no abstract content

36909598.model_family: machine learning on morphometric similarity networks vs. cortical thickness/volume features
36909598.clinical_problem: prediction of "brain age" during childhood/adolescent development from structural MRI
36909598.patient_population: healthy children (large-scale imaging database, exact size not stated)
36909598.model_description: Input is structural T1-weighted MRI; morphometric similarity mapping (a network-level representation of the cortex) is used to build predictive models of chronological age ("brainage"), benchmarked against single-feature models based on cortical thickness or volume.
36909598.headline_result: Morphometric similarity-based brain-age models did not outperform cortical thickness or volume models; all models were significantly biased by age but robust to motion

37218934.model_family: ResNet18-based convolutional neural network with regularized loss function
37218934.clinical_problem: mitigating the effect of biased/inconsistent radiologist labels when training a pneumonia classifier
37218934.patient_population: publicly available pediatric chest radiograph pneumonia dataset
37218934.model_description: Input is a pediatric chest radiograph with binary pneumonia labels; artificial random and systematic labeling errors are introduced to simulate un-reconciled multi-reader annotation, and a ResNet18 CNN with a regularized loss function is compared to a baseline CNN to see whether it can overcome the resulting label bias.
37218934.dataset_size: not stated (public pediatric pneumonia CXR dataset)
37218934.headline_result: Baseline model AUC dropped 0-14% under simulated label bias (5-25% error rates); regularized-loss model improved AUC to 75-84% vs. baseline's 65-79%

37268839.model_family: U-Net-based autoencoder / multi-task learning (MTL) / auxiliary-accelerated MTL (AA-MTL)
37268839.clinical_problem: bone age estimation adjusting for the confounding effect of sex
37268839.patient_population: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge dataset (internal validation) and 227 pediatric hand radiographs from Asan Medical Center (external validation)
37268839.model_description: Input is a pediatric hand radiograph; U-Net-based autoencoder, multi-task learning and auxiliary-accelerated multi-task learning models predict bone age while explicitly adjusting for the confounding variable of sex (by input, by output prediction, or not at all), with saliency maps highlighting discriminative regions by puberty stage.
37268839.dataset_size: RSNA Pediatric Bone Age Challenge dataset; 227 external hand radiographs (Asan Medical Center)
37268839.headline_result: Best RSNA test MAE 5.434 months (AA-MTL, input-adjusted); best external (AMC) MAE 8.190 months (AA-MTL, prediction-adjusted)
37268839.study_design: retrospective model development with external validation

37416843.clinical_problem: improving low-field MRI image quality for infant hydrocephalus treatment planning
37416843.patient_population: infants with hydrocephalus imaged with low-field MRI
37416843.model_description: Input is a low-field brain MRI/CT of an infant with hydrocephalus; a deep learning enhancement algorithm improves spatial resolution, noise and contrast-to-noise ratio between brain and CSF, with pediatric neurosurgeons rating original versus enhanced images for usefulness in treatment planning. Abstract text is poorly written/machine-translated in places, and the article was later retracted.
37416843.headline_result: Deep learning enhancement significantly improved contrast-to-noise ratio and apparent image quality as rated by three pediatric neurosurgeons (no single quantitative figure given)

37422163.clinical_problem: framing issue on the state of AI in pediatric radiology
37422163.model_description: Editorial introducing a focus issue of the journal on artificial intelligence in pediatric radiology ("The TRY-Angle Approach"). No abstract text was provided describing specific models or studies.

37425859.model_family: deep learning (fiber orientation distribution mapping from limited diffusion measurements)
37425859.clinical_problem: estimating white matter microstructure of the developing brain from limited diffusion MRI
37425859.patient_population: newborn and fetal brain MRI (two clinical datasets)
37425859.model_description: Input is as few as six diffusion-weighted MRI measurements of newborn or fetal brains; a deep learning model, trained using fiber orientation distributions (FODs) computed from multi-shell high angular resolution measurements as target, maps the sparse input to estimated FODs, validated across scanners/protocols and against post-mortem histology for the fetal case.
37425859.dataset_size: two clinical datasets (newborns and fetuses); size not stated
37425859.headline_result: Achieved comparable or superior FOD estimation to standard constrained spherical deconvolution methods while using significantly fewer diffusion measurements

37430748.model_family: multi-branch attention learning network with ambiguous (Gaussian-distributed) labels
37430748.clinical_problem: bone age assessment in East Asian children using ambiguous radiology-report-derived labels
37430748.patient_population: children (RSNA dataset, Western population; new China Bone Age dataset, East Asian population)
37430748.model_description: Input is a hand radiograph; a hand-object localization module and an attention-based region module identify informative regions using only image-level labels, and the network is trained with ambiguous labels (converted from radiology-report text into Gaussian-distributed labels) to output predicted bone age, evaluated on both a Western (RSNA) and a newly collected East Asian (CNBA) dataset.
37430748.dataset_size: RSNA dataset plus newly collected China Bone Age (CNBA) dataset (size not stated)
37430748.headline_result: Achieved competitive results with state-of-the-art methods and performance on par with experienced physicians on both RSNA and CNBA datasets (no single summary MAE given)
37430748.study_design: retrospective model development and external dataset evaluation

37508796.model_family: deep learning (region-of-interest detection network + classification network)
37508796.clinical_problem: identification of menarche status in adolescents
37508796.patient_population: 738 adolescent EOS cases (training/testing) and 259 adolescent EOS cases (clinical validation set)
37508796.model_description: Input is a biplanar (EOS) whole-body radiograph of an adolescent; a region-of-interest detection network followed by a classification network outputs sex and, for females, predicted menarche status, trained/tested with five-fold cross-validation and evaluated on a separate clinical validation set.
37508796.dataset_size: 738 adolescent EOS cases (development, 5-fold CV); 259 adolescent EOS cases (clinical validation)
37508796.headline_result: On the clinical validation set: accuracy 0.942, macro precision 0.933, macro recall 0.938, macro F1 0.935; for menarche status in females, accuracy 0.910, sensitivity 0.943, specificity 0.855, AUC 0.959, kappa 0.806
37508796.study_design: retrospective model development with separate clinical validation set

37610781.model_description: Editorial comment discussing a study on deep learning for detection of retinal hemorrhage on pediatric head CT. No abstract text was provided describing the underlying model or results.

37806973.model_family: support vector machine on radiomics features
37806973.clinical_problem: differentiating suppurative from tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis with nodal necrosis
37806973.patient_population: 101 children with cervical suppurative (n=52) or tuberculous (n=49) lymphadenitis
37806973.model_description: Input is contrast-enhanced neck CT of children with cervical lymphadenitis; radiomics features are extracted from segmented lymph nodes after dimension reduction and feature selection, and a support vector machine classifier outputs suppurative vs. tuberculous classification, compared against visual CT feature analysis by radiologists.
37806973.headline_result: SVM radiomics model: AUC 0.89 (95% CI 0.72-1.00), accuracy 0.88, sensitivity 0.78, specificity 0.90 in the test set

37807664.clinical_problem: automated detection of fetal facial anatomy on standard ultrasound planes for facial malformation screening
37807664.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal facial ultrasound screening
37807664.model_description: Input is a 2D fetal facial ultrasound image; a YOLOv5s object detection network localizes and classifies facial anatomical structures on standard facial planes, intended to help physicians automatically screen standard sections during prenatal ultrasound examination.
37807664.headline_result: Precision 98.3%/98.1% and recall 99.3%/98.2% (single-class structure detection and three-standard-plane structure detection/classification experiments, respectively)

37845455.model_family: hybrid convolutional neural network (trained on synthetic data)
37845455.clinical_problem: image reconstruction for near-infrared optical tomography to detect low brain oxygenation in preterm infants
37845455.patient_population: preterm infants at risk of hypoxic-ischemic brain injury (phantom-based evaluation)
37845455.model_description: Input is near-infrared optical tomography (NIROT) measurement data; a hybrid CNN trained on synthetic in-silico data reconstructs tomographic brain images, with generalization tested on phantoms with more varied surface geometry, inclusion shapes and detector arrangements than the training data.
37845455.dataset_size: phantom measurements (synthetic training data, no patient count stated)
37845455.headline_result: Substantial gains in reconstruction speed, localization accuracy and image quality even under varied measurement conditions (no single quantitative figure given)

38019888.patient_population: children under age 12 with limb fractures imaged by radiography at University Malaya Medical Centre

38083137.clinical_problem: automated measurement of fetal thalamus diameter to study effects of maternal factors on fetal brain development
38083137.patient_population: fetal 2D ultrasound brain images (1,111 landmark-coordinate pairs)
38083137.model_description: Input is a 2D ultrasound image of the fetal brain; FTDNet first detects the region containing the thalamus, then detects measurement landmarks via supervised learning to automatically compute fetal thalamus diameter (FTD), compared against a statistical shape model baseline using intraclass correlation coefficient against ground truth.
38083137.dataset_size: 1,111 pairs of landmark coordinates with verified thalamus bounding boxes
38083137.headline_result: ICC 0.734, significantly outperforming the prior statistical shape model approach and other baselines

38099931.model_family: AI-based bone age / bone health index tool
38099931.clinical_problem: generating bone health index reference curves for a non-Caucasian pediatric population
38099931.patient_population: 788 healthy Indian children and adolescents (bone age 2-17 years)
38099931.model_description: Input is a digitized left-hand radiograph; the existing BoneXpert AI tool computes bone age, bone health index (BHI) and standard deviation scores, which are used here to derive reference BHI percentile curves for Indian children, compared against existing Caucasian reference data.
38099931.headline_result: Mean BHI 4.02 +/- 0.57, mean BHI SDS -1.73 +/- 1.09; Indian children's mean BHI was lower than Caucasian reference, with the largest difference 21.7% (boys, age 16) and 16% (girls, age 14)

38223530.clinical_problem: quantifying regional brain volume loss in term neonatal hypoxic-ischaemic brain injury (HIBI) and cerebral palsy
38223530.patient_population: 297 children imaged for suspected HIBI; 96 children over age 3 with clinically diagnosed cerebral palsy and abnormal MRI underwent volumetric analysis
38223530.model_description: Input is brain MRI of children with cerebral palsy due to hypoxic-ischaemic injury; the NeuroQuant(R) AI-based volumetric analysis software segments and quantifies brain substrate volumes (intracranial volume, thalami, brainstem, hippocampi, putamina, amygdala), compared against a normative NeuroQuant database, across HIBI subtypes.
38223530.release_evidence: Described as "NeuroQuant(R) software solution", a named, trademarked vendor product
38223530.dataset_size: 297 children screened; 96 children with cerebral palsy analyzed volumetrically
38223530.headline_result: Average intracranial volume reduced to the 1st percentile of the NeuroQuant normative database in all patient groups (p<0.001); significant volume differences among HIBI subtypes

38881728.model_family: convolutional neural network regression (6D pose estimation)
38881728.clinical_problem: localization/pose estimation of 2D ultrasound planes in 3D fetal brain space, for training and guidance
38881728.patient_population: fetal brain ultrasound scans (transventricular standard plane acquisition)
38881728.model_description: Input is a 2D fetal brain ultrasound image; a CNN regression network predicts the six-dimensional pose (translation and rotation) of the imaging plane relative to a normalized fetal brain reference frame, evaluated for accuracy in localizing the transventricular standard plane used for fetal biometry, with data augmentation and larger training sets improving on prior work.
38881728.headline_result: Median errors of 2.97 mm (translation) and 6.63 degrees (rotation)

40337452.model_family: deep learning with geometric constraints (global + relative motion estimation networks)
40337452.clinical_problem: motion correction of fetal brain MRI slices for 3D volume reconstruction
40337452.patient_population: fetal brain MRI stacks (simulated training data at varying gestational ages)
40337452.model_description: Input is a stack of 2D fetal brain MRI slices; a deep learning model with a global motion estimation network and a relative motion estimation network (sharing features, weighted contribution) predicts arbitrary slice motion in a standard anatomical space, trained on a large simulated dataset of fetal motion trajectories built with a control-point-based simulation method.
40337452.dataset_size: large simulated fetal brain stack dataset (size not stated) plus real fetal brain stacks for testing
40337452.headline_result: Demonstrated state-of-the-art performance estimating more complicated and larger motions than conventional methods (no single quantitative figure given)
